skill.name: brewpage-publish
skill.description: Prepare local BrewPage drafts, publish approved content as a shareable link, or update an existing publication. Supports HTML, Markdown, JSON, files, static sites, and visitor response forms.
skill.summary: Draft, publish, and update BrewPage pages, downloads, and static sites.
skill.author: kochetkov-ma

security_audit.summary: The reviewed helpers send publication data to BrewPage and store reusable owner credentials locally. No evidence of malicious exfiltration, obfuscation, or prompt injection was found, but approval, archive review, private output, and receipt validation have gaps. The skill was reviewed without executing its scripts or contacting BrewPage.

remediation.issue: Direct invocation can trigger an external write without affirmative approval.
remediation.suggestion: Default to a local draft unless the user clearly approves the material, destination, and access. Require separate approval for a new publication after a failed update.

remediation.issue: Reusable owner credentials can enter transcripts or persist in workspace files.
remediation.suggestion: Use a host secret store or a verified private file handoff. Keep credentials out of standard output and remove deletion examples that put tokens on command lines.

remediation.issue: ZIP review can differ from the archive sent to BrewPage.
remediation.suggestion: Build the manifest from a structured ZIP parser. Reject ambiguous paths and mismatched member names, and apply the same credential exclusions to directories and archives.

remediation.issue: A link alone can cause REST to report success.
remediation.suggestion: Require a successful HTTP status and validate the receipt against the requested operation before reporting success or changing owner history.

remediation.issue: The hosted Page data example loads a versionless browser script.
remediation.suggestion: Document the runtime trust requirement and use a pinned release with subresource integrity when BrewPage provides one.

semantic_findings.title: Direct Invocation Can Imply Permission to Publish
semantic_findings.description: The prompt contract lets direct invocation with supplied material default to a live publish. Supplying material is not always an affirmative decision to send it to BrewPage or create a shareable link.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The default is explicit in the prompt contract. Local-only and ambiguous requests have safeguards, but the default does not require affirmative permission to publish.

semantic_findings.title: Private Recovery Can Return Owner Credentials in Tool Output
semantic_findings.description: The recovery command prints the full owner receipt to standard output after checking a command flag. A shared or logged tool channel can expose a reusable owner token despite protected file permissions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The flag gates the command, but the helper cannot verify the output channel. The receipt validation confirms the printed object contains a reusable token.

semantic_findings.title: ZIP Review Does Not Reliably Represent Every Uploaded Member
semantic_findings.description: The ZIP manifest uses a trimmed, line-based listing instead of preserving exact member names. REST uploads the original checked archive, so a manifest approval does not establish that every member was represented accurately.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The listing trims names and does not validate all members as canonical, unique paths. Byte limits and digest binding do not resolve differences between the manifest and the archive.

semantic_findings.title: REST Success Is Not Bound to HTTP Status
semantic_findings.description: The runner enters its success path when a response contains an HTTPS link, even if the transport recorded a non-success status. It can report a publication as confirmed without a valid success receipt.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Status is recorded at transport time but read only when the link is absent. No live service response was tested.

content.user_title: Publish Pages and Static Sites with BrewPage
content.value_statement: Turning a draft or static build into a shareable link takes preparation and careful access choices. This skill prepares local drafts, checks selected files, and publishes or updates content on BrewPage.
actual_capabilities: Prepare local drafts without BrewPage requests or tool discovery.
Publish HTML, Markdown, JSON, and files through a compatible BrewPage tool or authorized REST route.
Check a selected static build or ZIP and report its entry file and archive manifest.
Update an exact existing publication with authorized owner proof.
Prepare an HTML form and Page data settings for saving visitor responses.
Request a custom domain for an eligible HTML page or site with account owner proof.
limitations: A live write needs a compatible BrewPage tool or REST access. Local checks require the bundled helpers and their documented dependencies.
An unlisted link is accessible to anyone who has it unless the publication is password-protected.
File checks do not detect all embedded secrets. Review the exact files before approving an upload.
An update needs valid owner proof and the exact target. A site replacement also needs a complete build and a verified entry.

output_examples.output: The local HTML draft and private response settings are ready. Nothing was published or sent to BrewPage.

output_examples.input: Publish a reviewed Markdown brief as an unlisted link.
output_examples.output: The publication receipt confirms an unlisted link without a password. Anyone with the reader link can open it.

output_examples.input: Review my build before replacing my existing site.
output_examples.output: The local review identified the entry and listed the files. No update was sent. Replacement is pending your approval.

best_practices: Name the exact files, owner, and intended reader access before approving a live write.
Review the actual build files and remove confidential data or embedded credentials before upload.
Share only the reader link. Keep owner keys and management links in a verified private destination.
anti_patterns: Treating an unlisted link as private or restricted to named readers.
Uploading an entire workspace when only the built site is needed.
Retrying an uncertain write before checking its receipt or reconciling its outcome.

faq.question: Can I draft a page without publishing it?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for a local draft. Draft mode does not call BrewPage or discover publishing tools.

faq.question: Which inputs can I publish?
faq.answer: The skill supports HTML, Markdown, JSON, downloadable files, built static directories, and site ZIPs. Supported options depend on the route.

faq.question: Is an unlisted page private?
faq.answer: No. Anyone with the link can open an unlisted page unless password protection is active.

faq.question: Can I update a page without changing its link?
faq.answer: A content-only update keeps the existing reader link. Format or hosting changes can return a different link.

faq.question: Can a published form save responses?
faq.answer: Yes. Eligible HTML pages and sites can use BrewPage Page data. The owner can review private responses in the Data tab.

faq.question: Can I use my own domain?
faq.answer: Yes, for an eligible HTML page or site without a password. You need to control the hostname and have applicable account owner proof.
